newsitem.title: USA: Aroma of Cohibas draws U.S. celebrities to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Aroma of Cohibas draws U.S. celebrities to Cuba.

text.p: Cuba has secretly invited about 100 U.S. business leaders and celebrities to a $500-a-plate dinner in Havana next week to celebrate the 30th anniversary of the world-reknown Cohiba cigar, the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel reported on Monday.

As most Americans are prohibited from travelling to the communist-ruled island under a longstanding U.S. trade embargo, Cuban officials are tight-lipped on who is on the guest list. But published reports say movie stars Jack Nicholson, Danny de Vito, Matt Dillon and Arnold Schwarzenegger may be among those invited.
A box of 25 Cohiba cigars, known as Fidel Castro's personal favourite until the Cuban leader stopped smoking a few years ago, costs more than $800 in the United States, where Cuban cigars are banned.

The Cuban government will hold the dinner at Havana's famed Tropicana club on Feb. 28 to raise money for Cuba's health care system, the Sun-Sentinel reported. More than 600 guests throughout the world have been invited.
"To someone who smokes cigars it's like going to the Academy Awards," said Richard Sachs, a Boca Raton stockbroker who declined his invitation.

Under the 35-year U.S. trade embargo, most U.S. citizens except journalists and academics are prohibited from travelling to Cuba and spending money there. But one legal way to get around the travel ban is to be fully hosted by a foreign entity that pays all the costs of a visiting American.
"It is my understanding that everyone who is going is going legally," said John Kavulich, president of the U.S.-Cuba Trade and Economic Council, a private business group.

Last week, the Cuban government said it planned to boost cigar exports to 200 million in the year 2000, more than double the current level. The increase is possible only because of financing provided by foreign buyers like Spain's Tabacalera.
Gross income from cigar exports last year totalled more than $100 million, the government said.
